You are helping a user write SQL queries to a database. If something is not clear, you can ask the user to clarify what they need. The schema for the database being accessed is the following:

CREATE TABLE TV_Channel (
    id TEXT   PRIMARY KEY,
    series_name TEXT,
    Country TEXT,
    Language TEXT,
    Content TEXT,
    Pixel_aspect_ratio_PAR TEXT,
    Hight_definition_TV TEXT,
    Pay_per_view_PPV TEXT,
    Package_Option TEXT,
    UNIQUE (id)
);

CREATE TABLE TV_series (
    id REAL   PRIMARY KEY,
    Episode TEXT,
    Air_Date TEXT,
    Rating TEXT,
    Share REAL,
    18_49_Rating_Share TEXT,
    Viewers_m TEXT,
    Weekly_Rank REAL,
    Channel TEXT,
    UNIQUE (id),
    FOREIGN KEY (Channel) REFERENCES TV_Channel(id)
);

CREATE TABLE Cartoon (
    id REAL   PRIMARY KEY,
    Title TEXT,
    Directed_by TEXT,
    Written_by TEXT,
    Original_air_date TEXT,
    Production_code REAL,
    Channel TEXT,
    UNIQUE (id),
    FOREIGN KEY (Channel) REFERENCES TV_Channel(id)
);

When you have a final SQL query to present, always wrap it in a sql markdown code fence like this:

```sql
SELECT ...
```

This makes it easy to identify your answer. Only use one ```sql fence for your final query.

Here is a query to get the distinct TV channels that have cartoons associated with them:

```sql
SELECT DISTINCT t1.id, t1.series_name
FROM TV_Channel AS t1
JOIN Cartoon AS t2 ON t1.id = t2.Channel;
```
i need to know which countries these tv channels are from

Here is the updated query that includes the country for each TV channel airing cartoons:

```sql
SELECT DISTINCT t1.id, t1.series_name, t1.Country
FROM TV_Channel AS t1
JOIN Cartoon AS t2 ON t1.id = t2.Channel;
```
I need to check if these channels are actually playing the cartoons we're talking about.

To verify that these channels are actually linked to specific cartoons, you can query the exact cartoon titles and their original air dates that are associated with each channel:

```sql
SELECT 
    t1.id AS channel_id,
    t1.series_name AS channel_name,
    t1.Country,
    t2.Title AS cartoon_title,
    t2.Original_air_date
FROM TV_Channel AS t1
JOIN Cartoon AS t2 ON t1.id = t2.Channel;
```

This will return every cartoon listed for each channel, so you can confirm the specific shows and air dates tied to them rather than just seeing the channel names alone.
we should ensure the cartoons being aired are actually written by Todd Casey.

Here is the query that filters for cartoons specifically written by Todd Casey, showing the channel details and cartoon air dates so you can confirm the connection:

```sql
SELECT 
    t1.id AS channel_id,
    t1.series_name AS channel_name,
    t1.Country,
    t2.Title AS cartoon_title,
    t2.Original_air_date,
    t2.Written_by
FROM TV_Channel AS t1
JOIN Cartoon AS t2 ON t1.id = t2.Channel
WHERE t2.Written_by LIKE '%Todd Casey%';
```
